findings.title: Per-client resources suppress all-clients grants
findings.body: When a client-specific resource exists, this method evaluates only that resource; it consults the `Clients` all-resource resource only when the specific resource is absent. As a result, an all-clients permission stops granting access to a client as soon as any client-specific resource has been created for it, even if that resource's permission concerns a different scope. Evaluate the all-resource grant independently of whether the client-specific resource exists, so grants combine consistently.

findings.title: Existing realms are not given the new Clients schema
findings.body: Adding `Clients` here updates the schema definition, but `init()` returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, without adding the new Clients resource or its scopes. Upgraded realms therefore cannot create or evaluate client permissions because the required resource and scopes are absent. Add an upgrade/backfill path for existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: V2 client resources are not cleaned up when a client is removed
findings.body: The listener now runs only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, so a V2-only deployment skips client-removal cleanup. ClientPermissionsV2 stores client resources and their policies in the admin-permissions resource server, but provides no V2 cleanup path; deleting a client leaves those resources and grants behind. Clean up the V2 resource and associated policies on client removal without invoking the unsupported legacy `setPermissionsEnabled` operation.
